members.note: Number one. Organises the back four loudly and well. Works shifts at the port, so tell him fixtures early.
Came through our under-18s. Best one-v-one defender at the club. Electrician; misses the odd Thursday for call-outs.
Quick, brave, delivery improving every month. Final year of a sports science degree. Has said he wants to test himself higher up.
Screens the back four. On four bookings — one more is a ban. Talk to him before the Skerraby return fixture.
Captain. Eleven seasons here. Starting his coaching badges; shadows Niamh with the under-18s on Mondays.
Left-sided centre-half. Good on the ball, drifts too far from Dom when we are stretched. Ankle strapped since August.
Direct, quick, frustrating. Three assists in the last four. Needs telling to track his full-back.

brief.body:
Leading the press from midfield

What's going well: You have started calling the press yourself.

What to work on: (to finish after Hallowfen) You go on the wrong trigger — a pass back to their keeper is the cue, not a pass between their centre-halves.

What happens next: TBC. Talk to Aaron first.

members.note: Signed off the summer open trial. Sees a pass early and wants the ball in tight areas. Tight hamstring in September — managing minutes, hence the reserves night.
Top scorer two seasons running. Holds it up well, finishes early. Not interested in moving — new baby at home.
Two-footed ten. Takes every set piece. Teacher; unavailable for the half-term away trip.
Cuts inside too often for a left-footer on the left. When he goes outside he is unplayable.
Back-up keeper. Starts in the county cup. Excellent with his feet, still learning when to come for crosses.
Up from the under-21s in August. Covers every blade. Needs to slow down when he actually has the ball.
Thirty-minute player now and knows it. Scores off the bench more than anyone in the league.
Reliable. Third choice overall. Has asked about a loan for games — Idris to speak to Pellowick once their page is approved.
Plays either side. Keen. Gets caught square when the ball is switched.
Reserves captain. Would be in the first-team squad if he could train twice a week. Farm work comes first in harvest.
Back from a broken wrist. Ninety minutes in his legs again as of last week.
Signed from the summer trial alongside Reuben. Raw but beats his man. Next in line if a first-team winger is out.
Eight in seven for the reserves. Deserves a first-team bench place when Marlon is unavailable.
Shot-stopper. Distribution under pressure is the work-on. Trains with the first-team keepers on Thursdays.
Leaving for university in January — this is why we are advertising for a left-back. Great lad, will be missed.

brief.body:
County cup debut: what to expect

What's going well: You have earned this.

What to work on: Nothing new. Play your own game. Dom will be next to you and he will talk all afternoon — listen to him.

What happens next: Send once the manager confirms the squad.

members.note: Dominant in the air, reads danger early. Hasn't yet played ninety at first-team level; the plan is the county cup in November.
Tidy, quiet, never gives it away. Needs to demand the ball more.
Youngest in the group. Moved up from the under-18s in the summer. Runs channels all day; finishing will come.
Most gifted player in the building. Small, so he has learned to play half a second early. A scout from Greaveholme is in touch — handled through the club, Idris has said yes.

brief.body:
Alfie — goal kicks and playing out

Going well: Two saves at 1–1 kept us in it. Loudest voice on the pitch, in a good way.

Work on: Kicking off the floor. Their equaliser came from his goal kick going straight to their midfielder. He rushes it when the opposition push up.

Next: Ellis (first-team keeper) has offered twenty minutes with him before Thursday sessions for the next month. Short option to Deji or Tomasz first, long only when it is on. No blame for the goal — said so in front of the group.

brief.body:
Rory — body shape when receiving

Going well: Covers more ground than anyone, wins it back, set up Jude's goal with a pass most adults would not see.

Work on: Receives facing his own goal — Tobias counted nine times at Marrowby. When he checks his shoulder and opens up (see 73 mins on the film) he looks a different player.

Next: Shoulder-check game in every warm-up: I hold up a coloured cone behind him and he calls the colour before he receives. Told him and his dad on Saturday; both happy. Review after the next two games.

brief.body:
Jude — the next action after a miss

Going well: Six in five. His movement off the shoulder is the best in the age group and the finish at Marrowby was calm.

Work on: After the one-on-one he missed, he walked for ten minutes and we played with ten. He is hard on himself. This is about confidence, not effort — do not tell him off for it.

Next: Agreed a reset with him: clap twice, sprint to the nearest defender. Deji (captain) knows to gee him up. Keep it light. Mentioned to mum at pick-up that he is doing really well, because he is.
